behavior.absolute_numeric: Numerical-only first/second Abs derivative nodes evaluate to sign/zero for finite nonzero real arguments. Independent derivative and bytecode checks retain chain rules, original source domains, typed coordinates and ordered sources. Positive and negative zero refuse, including held zero-masked directions or weights. Public symbolic differentiation is unchanged.
behavior.global_values: A private Lipschitz enclosure handles continuous Abs compositions, with interval slope [-1,1] across zero and one-sided slopes on one-sided cells. It supports whole-cell centered bounds and monotone face reduction without claiming C1/C2 regularity. The exact C2 lane is tried first; only its precise absolute-corner refusal selects the alternative. All attempted work stays charged. Independent full-partition and feasible-point replay remains authoritative.
behavior.scalar_nsolve: The default scalar solver uses the admitted residual Jacobian for statically bounded closed sources involving Abs, sinc, tanh or coth. Dispatch admits at most 128 source instructions, 512 conservative derivative-work units, exact integers/intermediates within 53 bits and literal integer powers from -64 through 64. Other math sources retain the existing symbolic derivative path. Compiler, proof, domain, budget and cancellation failures never select a fallback. Original residual evaluation, exact-zero shortcut and typed output keys remain intact.
behavior.historical_artifacts: Ordinary canonical loading remains first. Only the exact native source-binding mismatch selects the complete historical Abs-to-abs lowering derived from the receiver's already admitted source. The unchanged artifact is independently admitted against that historical source. Only then are complete typed Expr::Function abs tags rewritten in its canonical export, and all retained evidence is independently replayed against the canonical receiver. Both residual/objective persistence formats and standalone/compiled-program root-proof replay use this path. No derivative proofs are regenerated.
behavior.accounting: All native admissions, exports, logical source-copy work and byte rewrites share the caller budget and cancellation. Legacy source copying uses depth-weighted work, memory and allocation charges. Bounded native .args ingress snapshots retain the existing Python source-capture boundary; this is not a physical preallocation guarantee for those snapshots.
boundaries: Numerical values and search candidates remain binary64 approximations.
Abs derivatives at an argument of zero remain refused; root, stationary-point and C1/C2 APIs do not gain nonsmooth certificates.
Global certificates prove an objective-value gap on the declared box, not coordinate-distance accuracy, uniqueness or a complete optimizer set.
The Lipschitz lane does not admit singular sqrt(Abs(x)) endpoints or unstable Piecewise seams.

Certified interval/global-value checks preserve their existing zero-base exclusion for held zero powers: Abs(x)^0 at x=0 still refuses in that lane. This is not a blanket value-only binary64 Pow(0, 0) rejection.
Historical re-export upgrades Abs tags. Mixed old/new lowering profiles and arbitrary source aliases remain refused.
Raw native/Session exact-source checkers remain unchanged. Migration is a bounded Python compatibility adapter.
Migration dispatch depends on exact static native mismatch messages; changed messages fail closed.
